name: Every Active Direction Contains a Seven-Vertex Three-Face
statement: For every active coordinate $e$ of an ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness, or of the underlying family of a rooted factor, there are coordinates $f,g$ and a coordinate three-face whose intersection with the family has exactly seven vertices. After projecting this face along $e$, exactly three vertices have both lifts. Consequently every nonempty one-coordinate reduction has at least three vertices and is not a cube.
proof: The convex-reduction lifting theorem makes the reduction $D$ nonconvex in the contraction $A$. Both are ample and $D$ is connected and isometric. The distance-two interval criterion for convexity therefore yields a square of $A$ with exactly three vertices in $D$. Those three have both lifts in the original family and the fourth has one, producing the seven-vertex three-face and the stated reduction constraints.
